$comment: DEMO / NON-PRODUCTION PORTFOLIO FIXTURE. Three DISPLAY-ONLY project records that exist so the Projects portfolio can be searched, filtered and sorted against a realistic register. They are NOT projects: they have no documents, no analysis, no buildings, no Option, no schedule and no journey. `src/state/projectAnalysis.ts` never sees them, so `demoProject(id)` cannot resolve one and `openOpportunity(id)` has nothing to open — non-navigability is STRUCTURAL, not a disabled attribute someone can forget. Every number below carries `syntheticPortfolioFixture` provenance and must never enter the pricing engine, Option state, offer output or a client presentation. Identity, address, client and manager names are invented; the images are synthetic and registered in design-system/assets/projects/manifest.json. Source: the approved asset/record pack artifacts/project-list-portfolio-redesign/README.md, with the manager assignment taken from the backlog ticket, which supersedes the pack's earlier table. LIFECYCLE: the field is `declaredLifecycle`, not a status these records are IN. A display-only record has no documents, no analysis and no Option, so there is nothing to derive a lifecycle from; its status is synthetic register data exactly like its areas, its value and its next meeting. `projectPortfolio.assertDeclarable` refuses `ready_to_pitch` and `review_required` here, because those two assert a state of the product no synthetic record can be in — a real project's status is derived by `src/state/projectLifecycle.ts` and never read from a fixture.
